title: Prominent Dimensional Effects on High-order Harmonic Generation in Strongly Correlated Electron Systems
authors: Kento Uchida, Shintaro Takayoshi, Yuta Murakami, Dongjoon Song, Alannah M. Hallas, Masayuki Watanabe, Takashi Konishi, Aiko Nakano, Koichiro Tanaka
abstract: Dimensionality strongly affects elementary excitations in correlated quantum materials, yet its impact on extreme nonlinear optical responses remains largely unexplored. Here, we combine high-harmonic generation (HHG) experiments on quasi-one-dimensional SrCuO$_2$ and quasi-two-dimensional Pr$_2$CuO$_4$ with nonequilibrium simulations of Hubbard models. We find a pronounced dimensional contrast: SrCuO$_2$ exhibits a robust plateau-like high-harmonic spectrum with weak temperature dependence, whereas Pr$_2$CuO$_4$ shows a monotonic decrease in harmonic yield and strong thermal suppression, especially at higher harmonics. The simulations qualitatively reproduce these trends and identify dimensionality-dependent doublon--holon dephasing, governed by spin--charge coupling, as their microscopic origin. These results establish dimensionality and spin--charge coupling as key control parameters for extreme nonlinear optical responses in correlated insulators.
summary: This paper explores how dimensionality controls the extreme nonlinear optical response, specifically High-Harmonic Generation, in strongly correlated cuprate insulators. By combining experiments on 1D and 2D materials with advanced Hubbard model simulations, the authors demonstrate that dimensionality dictates the coherence dynamics of charge carriers. The findings establish dimensionality and spin-charge coupling as critical control parameters for manipulating light-matter interactions in these complex quantum materials.
main_problem: The study investigates how the dimensionality of a strongly correlated electron system affects its extreme nonlinear optical response, specifically High-Harmonic Generation (HHG).
main_result: A pronounced dimensional contrast was found: quasi-1D $	ext{SrCuO}_2$ exhibits a robust, plateau-like HH spectrum, while quasi-2D $	ext{Pr}_2	ext{CuO}_4$ shows strong thermal suppression, linking this to dimensionality-dependent doublon–holon dephasing.
method: The research combines experimental HHG measurements on cuprates with theoretical nonequilibrium simulations using the Hubbard model (iTEBD and DMFT).
model_or_system: The physical systems are quasi-1D ($	ext{SrCuO}_2$) and quasi-2D ($	ext{Pr}_2	ext{CuO}_4$) charge-transfer insulators, modeled by an effective single-band Hubbard Hamiltonian. The dynamics are simulated using advanced quantum many-body techniques.
key_observables: High-harmonic generation (HHG) spectrum, temperature dependence of harmonic yield, and subcycle spectra revealing doublon–holon coherence.
important_parameters: Dimensionality (1D vs 2D), temperature (thermal suppression), and spin-charge coupling strength.
main_assumptions: The theoretical analysis relies on mapping the system to an effective single-band Hubbard model and using approximations like NCA in DMFT.
figures_summary: Figures compare HH spectra and temperature dependence for 1D vs 2D systems, showing the characteristic plateau vs. monotonic decay. Subcycle spectra illustrate the time evolution of coherence, which is suppressed in 2D.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem by contrasting 1D and 2D cuprates, presents experimental observations (HHG spectra and temperature dependence), and then uses nonequilibrium simulations (iTEBD/DMFT) to microscopically explain the observed dimensional contrast via spin-charge coupling effects.
why_interesting: The work provides a direct link between fundamental many-body physics (spin-charge coupling) and measurable, extreme nonlinear optical phenomena (HHG), which is highly relevant for understanding correlated quantum materials.

The dynamics can be decomposed into three steps: creation, acceleration, and recombination of D-H pairs. The lower panels show the dynamics of D-H pairs driven by an electric field in 1D (left) and 2D (right) systems. In 2D and higher-dimensional systems, the motion of DH pairs can disturb the spin background and generate spin excitations, indicated by green wavy curves. This illustrates the strong influence of spin–charge coupling on the charge dynamics. Right: Experimental results of HHG in SrCuO2 and Pr2CuO4.
